Initial node features are obtained from detected objects: for two-stage detectors, RoIAlign is applied to the image feature map and each detected bounding box; for transformer-based detectors, the transformer decoder’s object queries are used directly. These visual features are combined with each object’s box coordinates and class probabilities to form the initial nodes. [2,3]

Initial edges are proposed by scoring all node pairs using their boxes, class logits, and visual features, retaining the highest-scoring edges per node, and removing duplicates. For each retained edge, its box is the union of its endpoint boxes, and its feature is extracted either with RoIAlign over that union box (two-stage detectors) or by summing the two node features (transformer-based detectors). [3,4]

Finally, a latent-graph GNN takes the initial nodes and edges as input and produces updated node and edge features. [1]

[5] Its ablations are conducted in the bounding-box setting, although it can also use segmentation-mask annotations and gains 4.1 mAP relative to box-trained LG-CVS. [3,4]

SAM 3 is evaluated on public video benchmarks—LVVIS, BURST, YTVIS, OVIS, BDD100K, GMOT40, and DeepSeaMOT—and reports each dataset’s official metrics rather than a single stated mAP metric; for DeepSeaMOT, it reports the average across four subsets. [2] Its evaluation uses text prompts: for public benchmarks, every video is prompted with all dataset category names, while another evaluation setup supplies each video with its associated list of noun-phrase prompts. The SAGES CVS Challenge uses sparse temporal labeling: 18 frames per 90-second video, sampled every 5 seconds, with annotators self-reporting confidence for each clip on a 0–1 scale. [1] Its provided description reports confidence distributions but does not specify a separate validation workflow for accepting or rejecting annotations. [1]

In contrast, SA-Co/VEval applies explicit quality-control and validation procedures. For images, annotators verify pseudo-labeled mask quality, verify whether accepted masks exhaustively cover the phrase, and manually add missing masks until all concept instances are masked. [3] For video, individual responses are validated, and only annotations meeting the required quality criterion are retained. [3] SA-Co/Gold additionally records three independent annotator responses to capture ambiguity and measure agreement. [3]

Excerpt A trains a depth-estimation model to predict a depth map, ray map, and optionally camera pose, using a weighted objective that combines depth, ray-map, reprojected-point-map, optional camera-pose, and depth-gradient losses. [2] Ground-truth signals are normalized with a common scale based on valid reprojected point maps before computing these losses. [2] Its loss terms use the ℓ1 norm, and the gradient term matches horizontal and vertical depth gradients to preserve sharp edges and promote smooth planar regions. [2,5]

Excerpt B uses prototype contrastive learning to make class prototypes discriminative: prototypes act as anchors, same-class SAM-based embeddings are positive samples, and embeddings from other classes are negative samples. [1,3] The prototype contrastive loss is motivated by InfoNCE and is used alongside Dice segmentation loss in an end-to-end tuning objective, \(L = L_{\mathrm{DICE}} + L_{\mathrm{PCL}}\). [1,3] Thus, A is a multi-output geometric-regression objective based on ℓ1 and gradient consistency, whereas B jointly optimizes segmentation overlap and class-prototype discrimination through Dice and contrastive losses. [2,3,5]
